subject: social-studies
title: The Globalisation Supply Chain of One Smartphone

questions.prompt: A student says: A global product is made entirely in the country where it is sold, because every stage of making it happens in one place. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - the phone carries one brand and is sold in one shop, so it must have been made in that one place

A global product crosses borders at every stage: raw materials are mined in one country, components are made in a second, the product is assembled in a third, and only then is it shipped to the shop shelf in Singapore - value is added at every handover along the chain.
The phone was made entirely in Country A, because that is where the chain starts
Only Singapore mattered; the earlier stages added no value at all

questions.misconception: A global product is made entirely in the country where it is sold, because every stage of making it happens in one place.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: A global product is made entirely in the country where it is sold, because every stage of making it happens in one place. In fact A global product crosses borders at every stage: raw materials are mined in one country, components are made in a second, the product is assembled in a third, and only then is it shipped to the shop shelf in Singapore - value is added at every handover along the chain.

questions.prompt: In which country are the components made?
questions.explanation: Scene 2 works this: the raw materials travel to Country B, where factories turn them into chips, screens and batteries, and the value rises to $35.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state the four stages of the supply chain in order.
questions.answer: Raw materials are mined in Country A ($10), components are made in Country B ($35), the phone is assembled in Country C ($70), and it is sold in Singapore ($120).
questions.explanation: The animation runs the chain in that order, with a route arrow carrying the product from each stage to the next.

questions.prompt: Explain why the phone is worth more after assembly in Country C than it was as components in Country B.
questions.answer: Assembly turns separate chips, screens and batteries into one working smartphone, so the finished phone is worth $70 - more than the $35 of components - because a usable product is worth more than loose parts.
questions.explanation: Scene 3 shows the value bar rising from $35 to $70 as the components are assembled into a finished phone.

questions.prompt: Which list gives the supply chain in order?

choices.text: Country A mines ($10), Country B components ($35), Country C assembly ($70), Singapore sells ($120)
Singapore sells ($120), Country C assembly ($70), Country B components ($35), Country A mines ($10)
Country C assembly ($70), Country A mines ($10), Singapore sells ($120), Country B components ($35)
Country B components ($35), Singapore sells ($120), Country A mines ($10), Country C assembly ($70)

questions.explanation: The whole animation names the chain: one stage hands the product on, value rises at the next - Country A, Country B, Country C, Singapore.
